summary: The Prosperity pillar of the World Economic Forum's Stakeholder Capitalism Metrics: employment and wealth generation, innovation in better products and services, and community and social vitality. It has 5 core and 7 expanded metrics.

disclosures.title: Employment and wealth generation: Absolute number and rate of employment

questions.text: What was the total number of new employee hires during the reporting period?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: Adapted from GRI 401-1a (New employee hires) and 401-1b (Employee turnover), to include other indicators of diversity. Report the headcount of new employee hires. Part 1 of the metric.

questions.text: What was the overall rate of new hires during the reporting period?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: Adapted from GRI 401-1a (New employee hires) and 401-1b (Employee turnover), to include other indicators of diversity. Report as a percentage: number of new employee hires divided by total employees at the end of the period (GRI 401-1 rate).

questions.text: How do new employee hires break down by age group (e.g. under 30, 30-50, over 50)?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: Adapted from GRI 401-1a (New employee hires) and 401-1b (Employee turnover), to include other indicators of diversity. Give numbers and rates for each age group.

questions.text: How do new employee hires break down by gender?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: Adapted from GRI 401-1a (New employee hires) and 401-1b (Employee turnover), to include other indicators of diversity. Give numbers and rates for each gender.

questions.text: How do new employee hires break down by other indicators of diversity (e.g. minority or under-represented groups)?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: Adapted from GRI 401-1a (New employee hires) and 401-1b (Employee turnover), to include other indicators of diversity. Give numbers and rates for each diversity group you track. WEF adds this to the GRI requirement.

questions.text: How do new employee hires break down by region?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: Adapted from GRI 401-1a (New employee hires) and 401-1b (Employee turnover), to include other indicators of diversity. Give numbers and rates for each region where you operate.

questions.text: What was the total number of employees who left (turnover) during the reporting period?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: Adapted from GRI 401-1a (New employee hires) and 401-1b (Employee turnover), to include other indicators of diversity. Report the headcount of employees who left (turnover). Part 2 of the metric.

questions.text: What was the overall rate of employee turnover during the reporting period?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: Adapted from GRI 401-1a (New employee hires) and 401-1b (Employee turnover), to include other indicators of diversity. Report as a percentage: number of employees who left (turnover) divided by total employees at the end of the period (GRI 401-1 rate).

questions.text: How do employees who left (turnover) break down by age group (e.g. under 30, 30-50, over 50)?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: Adapted from GRI 401-1a (New employee hires) and 401-1b (Employee turnover), to include other indicators of diversity. Give numbers and rates for each age group.

questions.text: How do employees who left (turnover) break down by gender?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: Adapted from GRI 401-1a (New employee hires) and 401-1b (Employee turnover), to include other indicators of diversity. Give numbers and rates for each gender.

questions.text: How do employees who left (turnover) break down by other indicators of diversity (e.g. minority or under-represented groups)?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: Adapted from GRI 401-1a (New employee hires) and 401-1b (Employee turnover), to include other indicators of diversity. Give numbers and rates for each diversity group you track. WEF adds this to the GRI requirement.

questions.text: How do employees who left (turnover) break down by region?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: Adapted from GRI 401-1a (New employee hires) and 401-1b (Employee turnover), to include other indicators of diversity. Give numbers and rates for each region where you operate.

disclosures.title: Employment and wealth generation: Economic contribution

questions.text: On what basis and for which operations did you calculate your direct economic value generated and distributed?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 201-1 (Direct economic value generated and distributed) and GRI 201-4. Confirm it is on an accrual basis and covers global operations. Part 1 of the metric.

questions.text: What was your revenue (a) in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 201-1 (Direct economic value generated and distributed) and GRI 201-4. Report in currency. Part 1(a): net sales plus revenues from financial investments and sales of assets.

questions.text: What were your operating costs (b) in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 201-1 (Direct economic value generated and distributed) and GRI 201-4. Report in currency. Part 1(b): payments to suppliers, non-strategic investments, royalties and facilitation payments.

questions.text: What were your employee wages and benefits (c) in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 201-1 (Direct economic value generated and distributed) and GRI 201-4. Report in currency. Part 1(c): total payroll and other employee payments, excluding future commitments.

questions.text: What were your payments to providers of capital (d) in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 201-1 (Direct economic value generated and distributed) and GRI 201-4. Report in currency. Part 1(d): e.g. dividends, interest payments to lenders.

questions.text: What were your payments to government (e) in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 201-1 (Direct economic value generated and distributed) and GRI 201-4. Report in currency. Part 1(e): gross taxes and related penalties paid at international, national and local levels.

questions.text: What was your community investment (f) in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 201-1 (Direct economic value generated and distributed) and GRI 201-4. Report in currency. Part 1(f): voluntary contributions and investment of funds in the broader community.

questions.text: What was the total monetary value of financial assistance received from any government in the period?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 201-1 (Direct economic value generated and distributed) and GRI 201-4. Report in currency. Part 2 of the metric: tax relief, subsidies, grants, awards and other financial benefits.

questions.text: Which governments provided this financial assistance, and what types of assistance did you receive?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 201-1 (Direct economic value generated and distributed) and GRI 201-4. Part 2 of the metric. Optional detail: list each government and the form of assistance (e.g. subsidy, grant, tax relief).

disclosures.title: Wealth creation and employment: Financial investment contribution disclosure

questions.text: What were your total capital expenditures (CapEx) in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Wealth creation and employment · Source: IAS 7 Statement of Cash Flows, US GAAP ASC 230. Report in currency. Part 1 of the metric, taken from the cash flow statement.

questions.text: What was your depreciation in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Wealth creation and employment · Source: IAS 7 Statement of Cash Flows, US GAAP ASC 230. Report in currency. Part 1: needed to calculate CapEx minus depreciation.

questions.text: What is your total CapEx minus depreciation?
questions.hint: Wealth creation and employment · Source: IAS 7 Statement of Cash Flows, US GAAP ASC 230. Report in currency: total CapEx less depreciation. Part 1 of the metric.

questions.text: What is your investment strategy?
questions.hint: Wealth creation and employment · Source: IAS 7 Statement of Cash Flows, US GAAP ASC 230. Part 1 narrative: describe how and why the company invests, supporting the CapEx figure.

questions.text: What was the total value of your share buybacks in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Wealth creation and employment · Source: IAS 7 Statement of Cash Flows, US GAAP ASC 230. Report in currency. Part 2 of the metric.

questions.text: What was the total value of dividend payments in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Wealth creation and employment · Source: IAS 7 Statement of Cash Flows, US GAAP ASC 230. Report in currency. Part 2 of the metric.

questions.text: What is your total of share buybacks plus dividend payments?
questions.hint: Wealth creation and employment · Source: IAS 7 Statement of Cash Flows, US GAAP ASC 230. Report in currency: buybacks plus dividends. Part 2 of the metric.

questions.text: What is your strategy for returns of capital to shareholders?
questions.hint: Wealth creation and employment · Source: IAS 7 Statement of Cash Flows, US GAAP ASC 230. Part 2 narrative: describe your approach to buybacks and dividends.

disclosures.title: Innovation in better products and services: Total R&D expenses ($)

questions.text: What were your total costs related to research and development in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Innovation in better products and services · Source: US GAAP ASC 730. Report in currency. Total costs related to research and development.

questions.text: What percentage of your revenue do your R&D costs represent?
questions.hint: Innovation in better products and services · Source: US GAAP ASC 730. Optional context: R&D costs divided by total revenue, as a percentage.

questions.text: What types of activities are included in your R&D costs?
questions.hint: Innovation in better products and services · Source: US GAAP ASC 730. Briefly describe what you count as R&D (e.g. materials, staff, equipment, contract research).

disclosures.title: Community and social vitality: Total tax paid

questions.text: What was the total global tax borne by the company in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: Adapted from GRI 201-1 (2016). Report in currency: all taxes that are a cost to the company, across global operations.

questions.text: How much corporate income tax did the company pay?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: Adapted from GRI 201-1 (2016). Report in currency. Category of tax.

questions.text: How much property tax did the company pay?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: Adapted from GRI 201-1 (2016). Report in currency. Category of tax.

questions.text: How much non-creditable VAT and other sales taxes did the company bear?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: Adapted from GRI 201-1 (2016). Report in currency. Only VAT and sales taxes that you cannot recover.

questions.text: How much employer-paid payroll tax did the company pay?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: Adapted from GRI 201-1 (2016). Report in currency. Category of tax.

questions.text: How much other tax that is a cost to the company did you pay?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: Adapted from GRI 201-1 (2016). Report in currency. Any other taxes that constitute costs to the company; name them in your notes.

disclosures.title: Employment and wealth generation: Infrastructure investments and services supported

questions.text: Has your company made significant infrastructure investments or supported significant services?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 203-1 (Infrastructure investments and services supported). Qualitative disclosure. Answer No if there are none; later questions then do not apply.

questions.text: What significant infrastructure investments and services have you supported?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 203-1 (Infrastructure investments and services supported). Part 1: describe each one, e.g. transport links, utilities, social facilities, health and wellness centres.

questions.text: How far have these investments and services been developed?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 203-1 (Infrastructure investments and services supported). Part 1: extent of development, e.g. planned, under construction, operational.

questions.text: What current or expected positive impacts do they have on communities and local economies?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 203-1 (Infrastructure investments and services supported). Part 2 of the metric.

questions.text: What current or expected negative impacts do they have on communities and local economies?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 203-1 (Infrastructure investments and services supported). Part 2 of the metric: include negative impacts where relevant.

questions.text: Are these investments and services commercial, in-kind or pro bono engagements?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 203-1 (Infrastructure investments and services supported). Part 3 of the metric. Select all that apply.

disclosures.title: Employment and wealth generation: Significant indirect economic impacts

questions.text: What are examples of significant positive indirect economic impacts of your organization?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 203-2 (Significant indirect economic impacts). Part 1: e.g. job creation in the supply chain, economic development in low-income areas.

questions.text: What are examples of significant negative indirect economic impacts of your organization?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 203-2 (Significant indirect economic impacts). Part 1: e.g. displacement of communities, increased use of transport.

questions.text: How significant are these impacts compared with external benchmarks such as national and international standards or protocols?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 203-2 (Significant indirect economic impacts). Part 2: compare with benchmarks and protocols.

questions.text: How significant are these impacts compared with stakeholder priorities and policy agendas?
questions.hint: Employment and wealth generation · Source: GRI 203-2 (Significant indirect economic impacts). Part 2: relate to stakeholder priorities and policy agendas.

disclosures.title: Innovation in better products and services: Social value generated (%)

questions.text: What percentage of your revenue comes from products and services designed to deliver specific social benefits?
questions.hint: Innovation in better products and services · Source: Adapted from GRI FiFS7 and FiFS8, SASB FN0102-16.a, EPIC Report (2018). Report as a percentage of total revenue.

questions.text: What percentage of your revenue comes from products and services designed to address specific sustainability challenges?
questions.hint: Innovation in better products and services · Source: Adapted from GRI FiFS7 and FiFS8, SASB FN0102-16.a, EPIC Report (2018). Report as a percentage of total revenue.

questions.text: Which products and services are included, and what social benefit or sustainability challenge does each address?
questions.hint: Innovation in better products and services · Source: Adapted from GRI FiFS7 and FiFS8, SASB FN0102-16.a, EPIC Report (2018). List the products and services and the criteria you used to classify them.

disclosures.title: Innovation in better products and services: Vitality index

questions.text: What were the sales from products launched in the past three (or five) years?
questions.hint: Innovation in better products and services · Source: Adapted from OECD Oslo Manual Section 8.3.1. Report in currency. State whether you use a three or five year window.

questions.text: What were your total sales in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Innovation in better products and services · Source: Adapted from OECD Oslo Manual Section 8.3.1. Report in currency (gross revenue).

questions.text: What percentage of gross revenue comes from product lines added in the last three (or five) years?
questions.hint: Innovation in better products and services · Source: Adapted from OECD Oslo Manual Section 8.3.1. Sales from products launched in the past three (or five) years divided by total sales.

questions.text: How does the company innovate to address specific sustainability challenges?
questions.hint: Innovation in better products and services · Source: Adapted from OECD Oslo Manual Section 8.3.1. Narrative supporting the metric.

disclosures.title: Community and social vitality: Total social investment ($)

questions.text: What was your total social investment (TSI) in the reporting period?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: CECP Valuation Guidance. Report in currency: the resources used for the 'S' in ESG efforts, as defined by CECP.

questions.text: How much of it was cash contributions?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: CECP Valuation Guidance. Report in currency. A component of TSI under CECP.

questions.text: How much of it was the value of non-cash (in-kind) contributions?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: CECP Valuation Guidance. Report in currency. A component of TSI under CECP.

questions.text: What was the value of employee time given to social causes (e.g. volunteering)?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: CECP Valuation Guidance. Report in currency. A component of TSI under CECP.

questions.text: What were the overhead and management costs of your social programmes?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: CECP Valuation Guidance. Report in currency. A component of TSI under CECP.

disclosures.title: Community and social vitality: Additional tax remitted

questions.text: What was the total additional global tax the company collected on behalf of other taxpayers?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: Adapted from GRI 201-1 (2016). Report in currency: taxes remitted by the company on behalf of customers or employees.

questions.text: How much VAT and other sales taxes did the company collect and remit on behalf of customers?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: Adapted from GRI 201-1 (2016). Report in currency. Category of tax.

questions.text: How much employee-related tax did the company withhold and remit on behalf of employees?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: Adapted from GRI 201-1 (2016). Report in currency, e.g. income tax withheld and employee social contributions.

questions.text: How much other tax did the company collect on behalf of others?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: Adapted from GRI 201-1 (2016). Report in currency. Name any other categories in your notes.

disclosures.title: Community and social vitality: Total and additional tax breakdown by country for significant locations

questions.text: Which countries do you treat as significant locations for this disclosure?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: Adapted from GRI 201-1 (2016). List the countries and how you define significant.

questions.text: What was the total tax paid in each of these countries?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: Adapted from GRI 201-1 (2016). Report in currency per country.

questions.text: Do you also report the additional tax remitted by country?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: Adapted from GRI 201-1 (2016). The metric says to report it 'if reported'.

questions.text: What was the additional tax remitted in each of these countries?
questions.hint: Community and social vitality · Source: Adapted from GRI 201-1 (2016). Report in currency per country. Only if you report it.
